Home Made Might Be Better. So it’s 2014 and I finally entered the world of touch screen computing and like a good sucker, I dished out $28 for the Kensington Virtuoso Pro Pen 39526 WW (Stylus and Pen combo). It arrived before the computer, but I decided to examine it nonetheless to see what makes a stylus a stylus. First of all, I didn’t like the feel and weight of this item and the pen leaked on my finger. The pen’s tip is a heavy weight metal, which makes it good for writing, but when it’s flipped for screen use, the heaviness is on the top of the stylus (where the pen is) instead of at the bottom. I don’t like that type of imbalance for drawing. I discovered that this item is an overpriced do-hickey that anyone can make at home from practically anything that you have lying around the house. For the how-to video instructions on how to make your own stylus to suit your personal taste and/or needs you can check out the websites that I’ve listed below and/or read the summary that follows.
Our smartphone, computer, or tablet’s touch screen senses touch because our fingers produce electrons, hence sending an electrical message to the screen that allows us to write or draw. Therefore to make a stylus, we need something that will behave as a conductor between our finger and the screen. Metal is a conductor. Inexpensive good metal conductors include aluminum, a metal rod (such as an antenna barrel or metal pen), a paper clip, a naked copper wire, or the metal spring that’s inside an old pen. A wet sponge or Q-Tip can also conduct electricity and neither of them scratches the screen.

To design a scratch-free stylus, insert a strip of sponge or Q-Tip into a metal casing (such as an old pen or a slender antenna tube that you’ve cut to size). Each should fit tightly into the barrel in order to make a good contact and connection with your finger and the metal casing. Wet the tip of that sponge or Q-Tip and use it on your touch screen.

If you don’t have a metal barrel available, you can use a cheap plastic pen. Drill two holes, one on either side of the plastic barrel. If you don’t have a small drill handy, you can burn the holes through the pen using a heated ice pick or paper clip. Insert the sponge (make sure it protrudes through the pen’s tip and that it also makes contact with the holes that you drilled). The final step is to insert a paper clip or a stripped copper wire through the holes and the sponge that you packed into the pen’s barrel. Next, wrap the wire tightly around the pen’s barrel. When you write, make sure your finger(s) touch the wire, which will transmit your electronic touch to the sponge and your tablet’s screen. TERRIBLE instruction booklet .... I like the basic design of this -- the small sleek size, nice layout of buttons, large display. The radio reception seems to be decent, although mounting it on the wall is not possible in my area, since I have to turn it various directions to get a couple of local AM stations. Weather band reception is OK, as is FM reception.

That's about where my positive feelings for this little radio end.

It is way too difficult to set up, NOT with regard to the physical aspects of hitting the correct buttons in the correct sequence, but rather in terms of deciphering and understanding the instructions. The instruction leaflet, such as it is, is written in such small type that it's nearly impossible to read. I finally went to the Eton website and downloaded the instruction manual there, then "zoom"ed it so I could read how to set the time, store radio stations, etc.

Then there's the issue of the S.A.M.E. codes. I had never heard of this technology before I got this radio. NO WHERE in the included instructions is there any mention of NOAA, or even the "S.A.M.E." designation. On the Amazon product page, there is a mention of "S.A.M.E." in one of the product features bullets, and "NOAA" in another product feature bullet on the product page here on Amazon, but nothing that explains what "S.A.M.E. codes" actually ARE. The instruction manual tells you how to "Select the county" -- OK, so what does THAT mean? The instructions don't tell you that "Select the county" really means "enter the NOAA S.A.M.E. codes." You're not "selecting" anything; you need to know the S.A.M.E. code(s) for the desired area(s), and then ENTER those according to the instructions.

This was my first weather radio -- and I'm generally fairly good at figuring things out -- but this had me confused for a good 15-20 minutes while I searched via google for "county code," "weather county code," etc. Finally found the NOAA site and the codes, and entered the one for my county.

And I STILL don't know what "Setting Defeat" means. I mean, I know how to set it, and I can read what the manual says, but it doesn't really tell me WHY I might want to enable or disable "defeat," and what, precisely, it enables or disables ("ENABLE: Alert when receiving a message. DISABLE: Displays the message on the LCD when receiving a message" -- does that mean that when it's enabled, you DON'T get a message displayed on the LCD when receiving a message? What kind of Alert happens when it's enabled? the flashing light? the siren? what, precisely, am I "defeating" with this??)

I have no idea if the weather alert part of the radio works. We've had one National Weather Service-issued high wind warning here in the Pacific NW since I received and programmed the radio, and it didn't set off the alert -- no light flashing, no "message," nothing. I intend to take this along on an extended road trip this summer (reprogramming the S.A.M.E. codes along the route), and I figure I'll probably encounter some sort of "alert-able" weather event along the way. I'll update this review then if that part works.

Meanwhile, I'm giving this 2 stars -- it works pretty well as a compact "clock radio," doesn't take up a lot of space, and has decent reception. But Eton REALLY needs to do something about the instructions. The ones included with the product are useless, and the copy on the website isn't much better.

Horrible Reception in the Same Location Where Other Antennas Can Pick Up the Signals. My high hopes for this antenna were quickly dashed.

I am 43 miles away from the broadcast towers. I currently use the Marathon antenna (I use it indoors). The Marathon picks up all the major network channels perfectly except occasionally 1, and all the independent stations perfectly except occasionally 1. (It will pick up those 2 stations, but there is sometimes annoying pixelation and signal drops.)

So, after I read how this brand new Mohu Leaf Glide 65 Mile Range antenna was supposed to be so wonderful, I bought it, hoping I could get all the stations in perfectly.

It's awful! Placed exactly where the Marathon was placed the Leaf Glide cannot even come close to picking up as many stations. And yes, I made sure the amplifier was plugged in. And it is getting power. (It also could not pick up stations that cheaper/inferior antennas could.)

I moved the Leaf Glide to different spots, but no matter where I placed it it could not pick up stations that it should have been able to pick up. It picked up some stations, so I know the amp was working. I unplugged the amp and those stations were gone, so I know it is not a defective amp.

I know that when it comes to antennas people's results will vary. But for this $89 (current price) supposedly "new technology" antenna to fail so badly is a huge disappointment.

There is no doubt that this antenna will work perfectly for many people, if they are lucky when it comes to distance, terrain, height, interference, etc.

You would think in today's world of big technology there would be a way to broadcast signals that everyone can receive successfully.

My guess is that this antenna would only pull in 65 miles away if one had it outdoors, high up, and with clear line to the towers.

(I am in no way affiliated with the company that makes the Marathon. I am just a cord cutter trying to get all the stations received perfectly. If the Leaf Glide had worked I would have been so happy, and would have gladly done away with the Marathon since it is quite big and not the most attractive. The Leaf Glide is paper thin and not anything that would be something you would not wanna look at.)

The Leaf Glide is very easy to place. I appreciate that they included two easy ways to hang it: Either with white or black push pins or with velcro sticky dots.

If you get all the stations with this antenna you will love it.

Positives & Negatives. I bought my pair of Bluez 2S directly from AfterShokz company, and not via Amazon. Just like with so many things there are aspects to like and aspects to not like.

I will start with the negatives. If you are in a noisy environment, such as working out in an exercise room, the volume just is not loud enough or satisfactory at all. You need earplugs in the ears to get the satisfactory volume. Yes, earplugs. Of course, that defeats the whole purpose of buying headphones that do not go inside or cover your ears.

You can test this out by simply putting a finger in each ear and then you'll hear the remarkable level of volume change.

Because of the lack of loudness one can achieve in a noisy environment, I cannot recommend these (unless you want to buy earplugs and wear them at the same time).

The only other negative for me personally is the lack of a way to go back to a previous song, or repeat the currently playing song. (You can skip forward to the next song, but you cannot go back.)

The positives: These are comfortable to wear and very lightweight. The Bluez 2S offers the ability for decent call quality when using them to make calls. Microphones seem good (I have only tried this indoors, and not outdoors, so I cannot comment further on this particular subject.)

The Bluez 2S are very easy to operate.

In a quiet environment, volume is fine, and music quality is acceptable for this price point. (Of course you will not get the level of music quality or bass you'd get with a more expensive name brand headphones that go directly over the ear.)

So, for specific purposes such as cell phone calls where you want to keep both ears free, these are quite good indeed, offering good voice quality for both parties. (Pairing with my iPhone 5 and 6S went flawlessly.)

[[VIDEOID:d627772a0010114e2d1717866c6d430e]] I don't know how long stainless steel zip ties have been around, but I thought this was curiously interesting. The tool feels high quality and heavy duty. The issue is that I don't see the point if the tool can barely outperform the hands and a pair of scissors. When you squeeze the handle to tighten the cable tie, everything feels super tight, but when you release the handle the slack comes back. So the idea is to squeeze the handle until there is no more slack, until it's super tight, then you use the built in chopper to cut the excess cable. That's the idea, that's the intention of this tool. But in reality, once you cut off the excess cable, some of the slack comes back. In my demo, you'll see it barely outperforms me manually tightening it and cutting off the excess with a pair of scissors. That's only because it was awkward for me to wrap my arms around my camera and tripod to record what I was doing. When I did it off camera, my manual method was just as strong as the tool method. Bottom line, this tool and the ties help keep things in place, it doesn't provide a super tight tie. You can already accomplish this the traditional manual way with standard zip ties. Actually, zip ties with grooves will lock in place and keep the tension better than these stainless steel ties. The problem is that they are smooth. Maybe if they make these ties with a little grooves it would help. But then gain, if it had grooves to lock in place, then you don't need the tool. LOL! We're going in circles. Like I said in the video, seems like a solution to a problem we don't have. I'll give it 3 stars because it does hold things in place, and it is more convenient than manually tightening and then using a scissor to cut.

One word.... UNCOMFORTABLE.. At $160, I said Nah. At $120, I said let me check this out, and my instincts were right, this is a no-go. Brydge seems to be a legit aspiring company, but I hope they go back to the drawing board and add upper cases to their keyboard design. So that you can put your tablet in a case, then the case connects to the keyboard, a perfect example of this design is an iPad keyboard made by Yoozon, I just reviewed it, it is awesome. There is absolutely no fear of damaging the screen with that type of design. But as for this Brydge keyboard, one word sums up my experience.. uncomfortable.

So there are 3 issues with this design:

1. There is no case, your tablet is exposed. This is not a deal-breaker, I knew it going in. But understand nobody makes any cases for pixel slate. Even Brydge makes a bunch of cases for various ipads complete with slots cut-out so that they can be slide right into their hinge keyboards. But there are no such products for the Slate, so you'll expose it to scatches.

2. Light bleeding in the corner caused by the hinges. I knew this going in as well, but I was thinking maybe it's paranoia. At $120, I wanted to check it out. And honestly, playing with it did not ease my concerns. You don't see any light bleeding at all, but you do see it when you close it like a laptop and the hinge is applying its pressure. I tried to reproduce this light bleed by applying pressure with my thumb, and I could not get it to bleed. So this tells me the hinge is applying a tremendous amount of pressure. Right now, the bleeding goes away the moment it's opened, but by opening and closing constantly and daily, I fear one day the bleeding will stay lit because I've seen this issue on normal laptops.

3. The hinge is a very thin sharp metal. The padding is what prevents it from scratching your tablet. But the padding for one hinge was no longer sticking flush with the metal. It would get caught at times when I'm sliding in the tablet. Good thing I was careful because if you carelessly trust the product, it can scratch your tablet if the rubber gets caught and pulled. Hard to articulate what I'm saying, so I've attached a photo to show you the separation of the rubber from the thin metal hinge. After a couple of uses, it was a chore for me to carefully slide the tablet in because that rubber kept getting caught. A little disappointed that just one day into this testing, I already have to resort to glue?

Like I said... uncomfortable. Brydge, please continue to focus on rigid hinge keyboards. You're on the right path. This is what we want. We want rigidness and lappability, but please design a detachable case so that the case takes the brunt of the hinge pressure, as well as protect the tablet from scratches exactly like the Yoozon design I mentioned above.

Passthrough video quality bad, drivers bad, recording quality good. I purchased this HDMI Capture USB device to record a Windows desktop session. What I noticed is that the passthrough video quality is very bad. What is clear text coming out of the computer becomes blurry by the time it gets to the TV. What this means is that you can't keep this device plugged in permanently to record when necessary. You'd have to settle for plugging it in only when recording. Perhaps for gaming devices that have larger text and buttons, it wouldn't be a big problem.

This device can also be used to live stream by plugging it in to the USB port on your PC. A few problems here:
-- This is only USB 2.0
-- The USB port is also used as the power supply for the device. This means that if your PC doesn't provide enough power through its USB port (especially if you have an external drive plugged in to the device), you won't be able to use this function. They did not include those two-headed dongles to provide additional power.
-- The drivers are bad. I was able to get OBS to preview the device only after a lot of changing inputs around. VLC will not work with it.

What I do like about it is that while the passthrough quality is pretty bad, the resulting recording isn't. You can certainly tell that it is a recording, probably due to the video compression but all of the text from the 1080p desktop is readable.

I also like the fact that you can record directly to a USB drive with scheduled recording capabilities. The UI of the built-in software is straight out of VHS days but it does the basics of what you need. The convenience of being able to press record on the remote to start your capture means you can set up your PC how you need it without having to also manage your desktop recording software.

Clock that doesn't quite do what you need it to.. I thought I wouldn’t be picky when it comes to buying a new alarm clock; I mean, I owned a Sony Dream Machine (yeah, you too?) for over 30 years and that had minimal features! At least, that’s what I thought until I actually started looking for a new one.

When you look at the possibilities out there you start to think that perhaps I need:
- Bluetooth? It would be nice to wake up to a playlist I set up in my phone.
- Good sound quality? If I’m gonna have bluetooth, the sound quality needs to be good.
- Projection? It would be nice to see the time on the ceiling with the press of a button.
- Atomic? It would be nice to NOT have to manually set the time for Daylight Savings.
- Temperature/Weather? It would be great to know the weather when I look at the time -- especially if it is projected on the ceiling!

The Soundbot tries to provide many of these features but fail to put them together into one cohesive unit. It tries to be an alarm clock and bluetooth speakers but fails at both.

The Good:
- Great looking design. The wood look and the size, color and placement of time and temperature all add to a great look for the Soundbot.
- Impressive sound. As I’m currently searching for a bluetooth portable speaker (and have already reviewed a few), I pay special attention to sound quality. It’s comparable to the Jambox Mini.
- Touch controls. No buttons to detract from the wood look of the clock. The snooze, volume, and phone buttons are all touch sensitive.
- Time is remembered even when unplugged.

The Bad:
- The clock does NOT play a bluetooth when the alarm goes off. The workaround is to use your phone as the alarm, but what’s the point?
- No Next/Prev track buttons. The +/- buttons only control volume.
- Only one level of dimming. You can choose full or half brightness with the snooze button but it is still a little bright for me. I have to turn the clock away while I sleep.
- Alarm only has one sound: an annoying beep.

Tip:
The alarm clock can be set to go off every day (the alarm LED is solid, not flashing). When the alarm goes off, PRESS and HOLD any touch-sensitive button to disable the alarm for today. It will then go off again tomorrow.

Conclusion:
With the inability to use the bluetooth as an alarm tone, and without an FM Radio as an alternative, the Soundbot serves as a pretty poor alarm clock. You’re stuck with a simple beep. Without a next/prev track button, the Soundbot serves as a pretty poor wireless speaker. The good sound quality is the only thing it has going for it.

Great Portability, Okay Pictures, Poor Durability. I bought this camera for my wife last summer when she was in China. She was looking for something with less shutter lag than our last generation of Nikon and Canon digital point-and-shoots, and something cute and portable. The Panasonic DMC-FX30 is both of these things.

Out of the box it overexposed and undercolored things, but this was easily fixable after fiddling with the settings menu. Even set up right, photos using the flash still look too shiny whit, and photos taken at high ISOs are pretty noisy. The lack of a real viewfinder also makes capturing action clunky, but this is obviously in part an artifact of my preferences. This camera takes fine outdoor pictures, and the wide angle zoom allows for some cool shots and works well in confined (well-lit) spaces.

The camera is a small, precision-made jewel of a camera, with controls and buttons designed for smaller hands than mine; they fit my wife fine. We both missed the lack of a real viewfinder; pocket cameras seem to making an unfortunate departure from this useful standard (bright sunlight washes the display out, and it's easier to take a picture from your eye, as that's what you're composing with in the first place). The camera performed fine in its role as a city camera in Beijing, and for snapping quick shots back home when lugging the SLR around was inconvenient.

Now, however, we are in rural China for a year doing field work, and I was using the Panasonic as a backup to my Nikon DSLR. It was nice having a wide-angle lens in a pouch in my pocket when I had my normal or telephoto primes on the SLR. The Panasonic worked great in this role for 3-weeks, and then the automatic lens cap froze shut and wouldn't open, despite my coaxing, cleaning, etc. I finally just pried it off so I can still use the camera (I keep a business card over the lens in the soft pocket pouch), but let's say that I am not impressed with the camera's durability, compared to any other camera I've had, film or digital. It never got wet, dusty, dropped, or sat on; it looks brand new, but the lens cap won't work, and failed in a way that renders the camera useless to someone unwilling to take pliers to a Leica lens (failing and staying open would be preferable).

Anyway, if you're looking for a field or reliable travel camera, pass this one up.

Very limited use. As someone who works with cameras for a living, I tend to occasionally misplace/lose my lens caps. Having a one-size-fits-all backup like this claims to be, is therefore intriguing to me.
What I found however, is that this fits alright for smaller sized primes (such as those with a front element of 52mm), but a lot of my zooms or larger primes with bigger front elements are difficult or impossible to fit over. Rear cap was also somewhat of a hit-or-miss; I own E-mount, EOS, Nikon F, Minolta A-mount and Micro4/3 lenses, and none of them are too large in their rear element, but some lenses get wide right after the mount and won't allow a cover like this to squeeze over easily. Some of the smaller primes, especially pancake lenses like the Canon 40mm STM, really can't fit both a front and rear "cap" like this since the entire lens would be engulfed in one end or the other.
On top of all that, even if it DOES fit over your lens, I'm cynical as to how how useful it really is. The purpose of a lens cap is to protect the glass from two things: getting dirty and getting damaged. For starters, the material is soft and won't prevent a hard object collision. I'm not exactly willing to test that theory but considering I can press in and feel the glass through the cover, I'm guessing a hard object in your camera bag could still hit it and crack/shatter/damage it. Perhaps the rubber would soften the blow, but a real lens cap would prevent any blow from happening in the first place!
For dust and debris protection, perhaps it is a little useful, however this sort of material tends to attract a lot of static cling. Just leaving it in my gear bag for a bit, I'm finding dust and hair clinging to it like a balloon. Now, it is possible that means the dust/debris will stick to the cap and not your lens, which is useful, however it doesn't give me a lot of confidence to see stuff stuck to the thing I'm about to use to protect my lens from more of that stuff.

I suppose it's good as a backup in my gearbag in case I lose another lens cap and want something to keep dust off it until I get a replacement, but otherwise I'd strongly recommend getting a proper front and end cap for your lenses.

Huge Canvas Backpack-Style Bag. Most bags and backpacks I see available anymore are made of nylon or polyester blends and while they look nice initially and are easy to clean they have a bad tendency to wear quickly and fall apart. I remember canvas bags when I was young that lasted for years. This backpack/laptop bag is the first canvas bag I have seen in years and it is well made and is very large - most excellent for a college student going to classes or a hiker spending time in the mountains.

To get a fair idea of the size I decided to stuff this bag as full as I could. I was able to cram in two full-sized inflated basketballs and two junior-sized inflated basketballs, and I still had a little more room in the main compartment of the bag. This is a really large-capacity bag and is roomy enough to accommodate a week’s worth of clothes, some sporting equipment or a good many college textbooks and a laptop. I have not used a laptop backpack that has come close to being this roomy before now.

There are a good number of pockets inside and outside this bag. In the main compartment is a divider for securing a larger laptop but there is also a zippered pouch that’s ideal for pencils, pens, a mouse, power cords or other smaller instruments. It’s probably the most protected area of this bag and would be a good way to stash a mobile phone safely. There is a second small pouch on the inside that is divided up for pencils, pens and other small items. There are three exterior pockets as well, all of which are about the same size as the interior zippered pocket.

What is interesting about the exterior pockets is the fact that they have snaps and buckles, but the buckles are decorative and are actually held closed by magnets. So, there is never a need to fiddle with the buckles at all - just pull on them and they easily pull free from the magnets. There is a flap that closes the main compartment as well and this is also held closed by magnets disguised as buckles.

The main compartment can also be closed via a draw string inside, providing a little extra security for the items inside.

The whole bag is real canvas, not some polyester/nylon weave. I looked this bag over and found no loose threads, no uneven stitching and nothing loose or out of place.

This bag lacks only one thing - a reinforced bottom, which would be helpful if the bag is going to be used for heavier loads for a long period of time. I have no reason to believe that the stitching or canvas will fail, but it would be reassuring to have a leather base or an extra layer of canvas to reinforce. This is by no means a deal-breaker and is still the largest and most well-constructed bag I have used.

Another reviewer mentioned that there is no protection for a laptop in this bag and I have to agree to a point. The emphasis on this bag was construction and strength, not padding and protection. So, if using with a laptop be careful when setting the bag down.

This is arguably the best bag I have seen and used in many years for laptops or just as a generalized book bag. It is very large, has plenty of pockets and seems to be made well. It is not perfect but it is closer than most.

hole and run in one sock, socks are different lengths, very thin, but compression is OK. I use compression socks for my venous insufficiency and varicose veins. I use 20-30 mmHg nearly all the time, for a couple of decades now so I know what to expect and how they should feel. I replenish the socks often as they are not meant to last forever (the sock may hold up but the compression decreases over time). SO I am always on the look out for a decent compression sock. These are NOT IT. I will tell you why:

The compression on these is about right. No real complaint there. Very important to select a size based not only on your foot size, but also on your calf size. If deciding between the two, I would aim for calf size or go to a different brand.

They are thin in calf area. I sense these will lose compression sooner over later.

One sock has a hole it in it that I noticed as I put it on. A hole with a run! No good! Also, if that weren't bad enough..

One sock is way too long. It goes up over my knee nearly to my thigh. The other sock just goes to my knee (as it should). The socks SHOULD fit in such a manner that it goes to the knee, or just below. Not so far above that it is like a thigh sock. Makes them uncomfortable as the band will bite the skin.

Maybe I just got a bad pair or maybe there is a bad batch. Regardless, I am disappointed. I CAN wear them, but again they have a hole and one is uncomfortably long. '

To end on a positive, the foot is accurate for sizing. I have size 10/11 womens (8/9 mens) and the L/XL is suitable for womens size 8/12.5 and mens 8-14. I have room left over. Just also need to have a calf size within 14-19 range. My measurement is around 17"

The foot has a slightly padded feel.
Toe seam sits on top of toes and not at toe nail (which is good thing)
Since there are so many design and color change, then know that there are corresponding threads on the inside. This is a not a positive but it isnt necessarily negative either.. it is just a detail I find worth mentioning as it may mean that some people may catch a toenail on the interior threads.

If my sock didnt have a hole in it (and a run) and if the socks were the same length ending at or just below knee, I would have rated these a 4. But with the host of problems I can't recommend these nor will I ever purchase more from this brand.

They work, but not the best design. I love the idea of heated gloves as my fingers get cold when playing in the snow with my kids. My wife has a heated jacket that has a similar idea- there's a battery pack that gets wired up inside and then an external button that activates and glows different colors to indicate what mode it is in. This is the same thing, but on two hands (so double the battery packs and switches!).
The jacket version is vastly superior to this in my opinion. To be clear, it DOES work, but there are some design flaws that make it a little frustrating. For starters, the battery pack uses AA cells and not a USB rechargeable pack like other heated items in this style. That's fine, except that the pack is very bulky and hard to get to when you need to change them. There is a zipper pouch that houses it, and you have to really dig around with your fingers to get it out and in. And there's a good chance you'll have to replace them every couple of times you wear this. There is also a "master power" switch on the battery pack, which I guess prevents accidentally pressing the power on when storing the gloves as well as preventing background power drain. If left on, the pack will drain your battery even if the glove's heating function is turned off, so you need to dig it out every time and hit the switch (found this out the hard way).
Not only is that annoying, it is bulky and won't contour with your arm since it is a square pack. See the attached picture, on my arm that carries my watch, the pack creates this awkward bulge. And it isn't that the gloves are too small on me, in fact they are a bit big on me in every other way.
The LED on the gloves also aren't very visible when outside in the snow. I kept questioning whether or not my gloves were on or if in the wrong mode... a few times one had turned itself off perhaps by either the battery dying or accidentally hitting the button. Using them at night solves this, but what if you're outside in the brightly reflected snow? In contrast, my wife's heated jacket is visible.
I was going to give this 4 stars because it's just mildly inconvenient and still functional, but after using it a couple of times and finding the batteries are already dead, I decided against putting even more batteries into it and just using them as normal gloves. For that, you can get much better fitting gloves for the price.
So, if you really need heated gloves on the cheap, they're OK. But they really could be so much better.

And no joke, about 25 years ago a doctor gave me a pair of children's "yellow sunglasses"; the kind you'd win at a carnival game. And while I knew I looked silly wearing them, I also knew they worked. I managed to hang on to that pair for years until one of my kids finally broke them two years ago. So as I mentioned already, yellow glasses work in my opinion. I used to wear my old pair when the sun was at it's brightest. I've also brought them to work too. I spend about 20% of my time taking a lot of pictures under very bright lights (no flash, but still bright lights). I can't tell you how much these have helped with they eye strain. I suspect they might even help with computer screen eye strain.
And I really like this particular pair because they're flattering. They have a traditional shape, which looks great on many different faces. And the tortoise shell color looks nice too. The glasses have a little weight to them and feel well made. I would recommend them!!!

Uh, No. These Are Fine In Front, But Back Is Butt Cheek Escape Hatch. I originally got these shorts to wear around the yard when I do my yard work. We have a rather large yard so I am always gardening, weeding, and doing other work around the property. Having shorts like these seemed like a good idea.

FABRIC
The fabric of these shorts is soft and well worn. They will last a summer maybe.

STYLE
The style fits well and is actually big on me which surprised me. At least in the waist and hips I mean. The 2XL in other clothing has barely fit my kid who is a size 12, so I got the 2XL expecting them to be small. They aren't.

LENGTH
Look, I am a clothing designer and have made and designed clothing for a long time. When you have shorts that fit the way they are supposed to, the front is shorter and the back edge is supposed to be LONGER to cover the larger area of the buttocks. You are not supposed to cut them off at the same length.

These shorts are ridiculous. The front is okay, but the back exposes the rear. If that is what you want, then you will like these. I don't. I like to keep my underwear to myself.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These shorts fit well on top but the legs are cut off wrong. They expose the rear a lot. The front is okay. The only way I would wear these is with bike shorts under them. I don't see myself doing that any time soon.

MY RATING
TWO STARS. The fit on top is nice, IF they had cut off the back tapered longer than the front edge, these would look much nicer, especially in larger sizes. As they are, they are awful unless you like showing your rear. I do not.

If I have some time in the future, I will alter them into something fun, but I won't be wearing them as they are.

Narrow In Hips, Short Sleeves- But Okay Coat For The Money. My favorite down coat ripped so I have been looking for a long version to replace it.

COLOR
The color of this is black- think shiny black like a lawn bag. It has a muted gold lining which is actually nice looking.

STYLE
The style is nice and basic.

FILLING
The filling is a bit less than other down coats I have used or tried on but it is decent.

SIZING
The sizing of this coat is okay with some issues. I wear a size 14-16 misses US and this coat fits but then there are a couple of issues. The size I am referring to is the XL size.

SLEEVES
The sleeves are too short. I mean my arms are so short that when I but something with 3/4 sleeves, my arms have the sleeves usually hit at the wrist like full length. These sleeves are an inch at least too short. There is elastic snapped cuffs and my wrists are bare when I am wearing this.

HIPS
The rest of this coat is roomy and nice, but the hips are way too snug. I am not out of proportion in sizing, so usually if the rest of the coat is roomy then the hips are too. Not in this case. I can zip up the coat but it is a bit snug in the hips.

WARMTH
When it gets frigid cold, this coat will need a few layers under it- thin layers. With the snug hip area that can be an issue. I can work with it, but it is frustrating.

ZIPPERS AND POCKETS
The zippers and pockets are great quality. They all work, and the pockets are deep and at the perfect angle.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This coat is nice looking, is plenty warm for average use, and has decent zippers and pockets. The sleeves are too short and hips too snug, so when trying to layer, it could be a problem. If you have REALLY short arms and narrow hips, you might do well with this.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. I like this but don't love it. I wear it often as a casual coat, but for really frigid weather, I will have to use another coat as it is a bit too narrow in the hips and cold at the wrists to be good for me.

PHOTO
My camera is messed up and I can only take up close pics without full length ability right now. If that changes soon (I hope so) I will try to post a photo for you. It does look just like the photos with this listing though, so if you need to know- they are accurate.

Getting only 89% of what I was supposed to. I got 89 beads. I contacted the seller. He offered an 11% discount. Even if I hadn’t gotten these through the VINE program, that would’ve been $1.67 back (sales tax included). Listing:

“Mixed Color Rhinestone Charms Beads”

My leggings that I LOVE are cotton 90%, spandex 10% and they definitely feel far more “cottony” than this garment. Honestly, they’re really comfy and you wouldn’t know about that spandex part.

If something from China is selling here, the sizes need to be translated correctly; otherwise, don’t enter the market. It only frustrates consumers and wastes time and money.
Otherwise, the style looked like it would be nice, and the fabric was delightfully soft, though the tag says there is no silk content, so the listing should not say “silk satin”. Silk refers to the fiber content, specifically strands made by silk worms. Note: I’m not partial to silk anyway, since it’s usually taken by very cruel means, so it’s great that it’s not silk. The problem is that the claim does not match the truth. It’s satin (type of weave). But it’s not silk.

Within a week of my putting on the bed, one of my children spilled juice on my bed. I was able to quickly strip the bed to put everything in the wash and the mattress was just perfect. Washing the protector was easy and putting it back on the bed went flawlessly. Highly recommend!

Nice quality heat resistant tongs, work perfectly!. These are great heat resistant tongs. I have been using them on my grill and just this past weekend used them to flip some ribs and chicken. No melting of the silicone, stood up well. I also love the red design as it matches my kitchen decor perfectly. This tool is well made (quality), fits great in my hand and maneuvers easily. It should stand up to years of use (with a little care).

Best insulated tumbler on the market!. I live in a golf cart community in Florida and I had been looking for some kind of insulated cup to be able to use both in my cart, to take to the gym or even just laying out by the pool in the hot Florida sun. I love this cup. It keeps my beverages cool (it takes a while for the ice cubes to even start to melt), it's a great size and holds a lot, and my drinks taste fresh and clean. I pop this in the dishwasher (along with the cap and straw) and it comes out sparkling clean. Highly recommend this insulated cup.

Fantastic pillow! Best I have ever used.. I absolutely love this pillow. I have suffered from neck and shoulder pain for most of my life and have tried all kinds of pillows to aid in my sleep. This inflatable cervical adjustable pillow is fantastic. With a touch of a button I can adjust the volume and get the optimum sleep support that I need. Material is super soft and cushiony but it gives me the support I need. I wish it wasn't made in China (prefer to buy American) but this pillow is definitely one of the best I have ever tried.

Great sheets, fits perfect and is super soft!. This is a really nice deep pocketed sheet set. I got a queen size and it fits my bed perfectly. I have washed this set twice since I have received it and the gray color is still vibrant and the sheets are virtually wrinkle free. These sheets are super soft and luxurious and I have already purchased a set for my son and daughter in law because I was so impressed. Spoil yourself (at a reasonable price) and buy a premium set of sheets for an optimal night's sleep. Highly recommend!

One of the best chef knives on the market today!. I love to cook and I am always in the market for knives. This Wallop Damascus Santoku Knife is just perfect. For under $80 (which was the price when I was reviewing this), this knife is as good as the multi-hundred dollar+ competitor knives. First, it a perfect fit in my hand which allows me to maneuver the knife around my vegetables smoothly and flawlessly. Second, it is super sharp and slices through tomatoes and onions flawlessly. I can honestly say this is one of the finest chef knives I have ever used and I highly recommend this knife for anyone who loves to prepare and cook. This also makes a great gift with it's attractive packaging and would be a wonderful, thoughtful, shower, wedding or homeowner present for the person you love!

Great smaller size bakeware, perfect for quiches. I love Chefmade products and have a lot of their baking dishes in my kitchen. This 7 inch tart pan is great. Well made, sturdy and easy to use, I can make a quiche or a small cheesecake easy with the removable bottom. Really nice looking to, it would make a great extra gift for a bridal shower (a size and type of kitchen accessory that may not be typical but truly will be one of the most used items in their kitchen). Really nice, highly recommend.

Wonderful way to enjoy your meals on the go!. Such a unique product! I typically bring lunch with me to work instead of buying it. Many times I have left overs (like yesterday I brought some meatloaf with me), but the sandwiches are cold by the time I get to eat them. Now with this little handy device I can plug in the bag about an hour before lunch and, presto, my lunch is warm and tasting fresh. I have already bought one for my son (who also brings his lunch/dinner with him on occasion) and will most likely give one as a gift this Christmas for a dear friend of mine up north. This is the kind of thing that would make a great gift for the person who has everything. Unique, classy and works!

Great small non-stick pan for muffins or candies. They call this a mini-muffin pan, but I think it is better for making candies (too small for muffins I like to make). Anyway, well made, beautiful color, easy to clean, this is a great cooking pan for any chef to have in their kitchen. A few of these in different sizes would make a great bridal shower gift to give to someone as unique gifts. Really loved this!

Well made, easy to clean, great for candy making!. This is a great pan for making small cookies or candies. Heavy, well made and easy to clean, this is a great way to make smaller sized treats for your family and friends. I especially like this for chocolates and have made several batches already and clean up is a breeze (practically rinses clean without needing a sponge). I highly recommend this pan for you or the chef in your life. Keep in mind the size of the cookies/candies when selecting this pan.

Really nice addition for any bedroom!. Very attractive, good quality, reasonably priced comforter/duvet cover. With matching pillowcases and a vibrant color, this is an attractive addition to my guest bedroom. For less than $50, it's a great deal comparable to famous name-brand bed sets. I don't know what other reviewers had negative things to say, this is a great product for any home.

Great tree skirt, inconvenient way to light. I need to start by saying I really am impressed with this skirt. It is large and a beautiful red plaid color. I kind of like the faux fur (might be a tad gawdy). This is really well made and a quality item. I deducted one star because of the lights and the way they did the battery. I actually turn my lights on my tree remotely now, however with this skirt, I need to bend down, find the switch and turn it on and off. Anyway, I will only be lighting it on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day as it is too difficult to put the lights on the skirt. They really should have thought that through.

A great addition to any kitchen, I couldn't think of an easier, tastier way to cook for my family. These are my absolute favorite items to keep in my kitchen pantry. I use my slow cooker at least 2-3 times a month and these liners make cleanup an absolute breeze. There is no easier way to cook on the planet besides using the cooker and the liners together. I was originally a little leery about using them, wondering if there would be any impact on the taste of the foods. But Reynolds truly knows how to make quality products that make our lives simpler and easier. If you are going to a bridal shower or a first time apt/homeowner, these would make a great gift (of course with a slow cooker).

Great pot holders, durable and long lasting!. I love DII products. Usually very reasonably priced, the quality can't be beat. These pot holders are no exception. Well made, they stand up to heat easily to protect my hands from oven and bakeware. I have washed them once in my washing machine and they came out looking like they were new. I love this whole product line as the colors match flawlessly and make my kitchen look clean and fresh. These would make a great shower gift to give the new bride (or even home/apartment dweller) as a complete set for the kitchen. Can't go wrong, great price and quality!

Great animal print cup cake cups!. These are super cute. I ordered them when I was making cupcakes for a preschool 'What animal would you like to be' party for my grandson. Colorful, different, unique. I love the fact that you can purchase theme-based baking cups like this. In addition to being unique, they are also practical and produce perfectly shaped cupcakes. Perfect for any stylized party needs you might have.

Absolutely gorgeous large countertop oven!. Beautiful addition to my kitchen. I must preface this that this is replacing another Oster oven I have had for about 2 years that is a tad larger. I will probably miss that I won't be able to cook the same size roasting chickens, etc, in this. But overall I am thrilled. I absolutely love the French doors. My old one had a door which opened down and could occasionally burn me if I wasn't careful putting food in or even simply closing it again. The French doors work in tandem and close flawlessly. I also think this unit is more energy efficient as well as my kitchen doesn't seem to warm up the way it did when I had my old counter top Oster going. No complaints, beautifully modern and looks wonderful on my countertop!

Another great Crock Pot product!!!. This is one of the best slow cookers around. Love the programmable (not just high-low) setting capability, love the size (perfect for when I am making a meal for four people), easy to clean and very attractive for the countertop. You can't go wrong with this purchase.
Essentials for any cook!. For the price, these are great wok accessories. Well made, super reasonably priced. I couldn't be happier. Goes with my new Aroma wok perfectly!

Great large oven!. I absolutely love this oven. To give you some background, I moved to my new home in Florida last year. With limited resources, I replaced many of the outdated appliances. The one thing I didn't replace was the range/oven. It was a nice gas/electric combo and appeared to be in good shape. Anyway, after using it for about 6 months, I woke up to find the range top working fine (burners) but the inside oven broken. I had to repair guys out here told me it would cost close to $1000 to fix (something to do with needing a mother board). Anyway, long story short, I had been depending on my medium size toaster oven to take the place of the large oven until I can try to replace it. I find it too small for larger things (think an oven roaster chicken). When I saw this Oster, and it was less than $100 (Amazon Warehouse deal), I jumped on it. It is beautiful (stainless steel blends well with my other kitchen appliances), the digital display is clear, large and makes it appear very modern. The size is great, I can fit a chicken in here with no trouble. I will most likely still need to replace my oven (think Thanksgiving), but this will get me through the next 7 months until such time as I can save up for the real thing.

Not what I was hoping for. Not a big fan of this. Bought it for cooking French fries and fried chicken. Fries worked well (although a little soggy so I had to take them out, pat them dry, and refry them for a bit. I had also hoped I could do the chicken, but this unit is too small. I mean, I was able to squeeze one nicely sized breast in here, but I found it ended up burning/over cooking the outside and after25 minutes was still pink on the inside (so I ended up finishing the chicken in the oven (ala shake and bake style). Anyway, if you are looking for something small, to do something small, this may be for you. It is cute and looks well made. However, there are no adjustments to the temperature (one temp fits all).

Beautiful piece for the bathroom. Love this tissue holder. First it is substantial and heavy (not made cheaply). The color blends wonderfully in my cream colored and pastel guest bathroom. I have ordered more to match this piece from the collection (i.e. the wastebasket and cup). I will be doing reviews on them when they arrive this week. I have nothing bad to say, InterDesign makes a quality product.

Good news - bad news. First, the size of this set is large. It is wonderful for cooking, straining and storing pasta. It is handy to have as it does all three (no need for a separate strainer) and stores nicely in my pots and pans cabinet. I was disappointed as I did try to store the pasta with sauce in the refrigerator. When I used the remainder I was surprised to see how easily the bowl stained from the red sauce. Several dishwashing loads later, it has faded some but I still can see it. I guess the lesson here is don't store spaghetti sauce in anything plastic (and I already should have known that). Outside of my own stupidity, this is a great set. I just wish the manufacturers would find a way to make these items a little more resistent to staining (for people like me).

Nice litte steamer with flaws. I was excited when I saw this in the Vine newsletter. I was traveling to Florida last weekend and wanted a travel steamer to take with me for the trip. For pros, this is complact and attractive and does create steam (although not consistently. I am rating this as three stars because it had a propensity to leak (thank goodness I wasn't using this on silk). I was disappointed to say the least and although it did the trick on the few pants and shirts I had, I had them spotted with water (but fortunately did not stain anything when it dried).

Great alll purpose countertop oven. Not sure why some folks found the dials complicated on this. I thought the B&D Rotisserie Toaster Oven a compact toaster over loaded with tons of features and bells and whistles (and I had no trouble figuring it out). Although I am sure the main purpose of this oven is to serve your toasting needs, I found the size large enough to bake pizza and even a full rack of blueberry muffins. I tried the rotisserie feature this past week and found it to be a little messy (so I do not think I will be using that again). However, what a great little dorm room oven/toaster to give a new college bound child! The stainless steel features match my kitchen design perfectly and I will be using this smart little oven on a regular basis (saving $$ by not having to fire up a full stove for smaller baking needs). I highly recommend this oven for everyone who is looking for a nice sized, multi-purpose countertop oven.

Basic Toaster Oven, no bells and whistles. This is a regular toaster oven, reasonably priced which does the job well (despite some of the negative feedbacks on here). I had no problem using this for evenly toasting and having consistent heating. The toast came out perfect. I also used this for baking some items (i.e. frozen pizza and some cinnamon buns) and I had no issues. I think this oven is a little cheaply made, and I have fears that over time the door may loosen and unhinge, but I guess you get what you pay for. It's stylish looking and compact, fits well on my countertop. Only 4 stars as it is basic and does the job. For $10-20 more you could do better in a Cuisinart model.

Good Grips - Great cooking!. I have bought several OXO products in the past and love all of them. They are quality made, durable, and made with the user in mind. The cookbook holder is convenient for me to us. Holds large as well as small cookbooks easily and is easy to position for the best visibility. Now that I have an IPad, I have also used it several times to accomodate the cookbooks that I have on Kindle for viewing. I love that this item can be folded flat for storage but, to be honest, I leave it out on my countertop almost all the time (I love displaying the books and with the OXO they look great open to Tuscan recipes and pictures). I have bought one of these for my daughter in law and plan to give it to her as one of Christmas gifts this year. For anyone looking to buy something to a new young bride, I would highly recommend it. Wonderful addition to any chef's gourmet kitchen!

A good entry level set for the new bride. Let's start with the pros: this is a large set with almost every kind of knife you could need (and even scissors), it's attractive and professional to look at on the countertop. Here are the cons: set is poorly made and the knives get marks/discolorations on them after several runs through the diswasher, handles feel loose and almost wobbly when using them for chopping, they only remain sharp for a short period of time (I found myself sharpening them after only two uses of dicing vegetables. I think this is a great entry level set for a bride-to-be and would look great as a relatively inexpensive shower present. However, if you are a serious cook (such as I consider myself to be) save your money and invest in a good steak knife set (which will cost over $200). It's like they say, you get what you pay for. It's attractive, but not functional.

Great baking stone. Having returned from a cooking trip to Italy last May, I was anxious to start utlizing my recently learned skills. Making desserts and pizza were two of the things that I couldn't wait to try when I got home. I first used the Emile Henry baking stone for pizza and I really loved it. The thin crust I made came out crispy and evenly cooked (475 degrees), my sons loved it. Only complaint I had was that it is not the easiest item to get in and out of the oven (especially when it is fully heated). First time I tried it, I found it heavy and almost impossible to get a good grip on (especially with baking mitts on). Stone also retains heat for a good amount of time (keep that in mind if it is summer and you take it out of the oven to cool). Second time I used it was kind of like a quasi-cookie sheet. I made biscotti which requires to bake the cookies twice (first time in a lengthy roll of almost 12 inches, second as sliced in cookie slices). I only had the oven at 350 this time and the size of the stone was perfect and the cookies came out delicious. I do highly recommend the stone for anyone looking for an extra tool in the kitchen. Cooks evenly, but might be a little awkward in maneuvering it when it is fully heated.

It really "sucks". What a wonderful cordless vacuum cleaner. Love the two power settings. Easy to use. Order for office because we had carpet only on stairs. It worked so well that I bought one for my husband for his boat and our cars.
Lovely absorbent coasters!. These are lovely! Perfect for my beach summer decor- then perfect for winter white! Love them!

Love it!. Ok this is a great little gadget! (I am an adult with no children) and I love it! I already made my own “Uncrustables”! The seller also sent a great little PDF recipe book! Three different sets/ shapes come in the order and They are so easy to use and clean.! Super happy!

Great pillowcase, and soft on your hair!. Where has this pillowcase been all my life?! I got my hair cut, and my stylist said "Your hair is really dry and coarse in the back" I told her it always has been- just in that spot- & she told me to get a silk pillowcase- because otherwise, we rub our head all around when we sleep and it is hard on our hair & it breaks it and damages it. With silk- (and satin- but she said silk is better) your hair will slide. This damage can also happen with car headrests. The pillowcase is very soft and nice. Now I just need one for my car! Like a silk bucket seat headrest cover! (Hint hint Alaska Bear!)

I love these bags. I am so happy to have finally gotten these bags after looking at them for a couple of months. They work well and of course I am happy to be putting less plastic in the landfills. They seem like they will hold up well and I like the different sizes.
Doesn't work. This leaks and it does not chop the food like it's supposed to. Returned!

LEAKING. I ordered this for a margarita party. It started leaking the minute I put the margarita mix in the machine. The mix did not stay frozen, melted right away, but I guess that is because it was leaking so badly. In addition, It was very hard to get it working. The blinking red light would not stop. When we finally got the light part fixed and turned it on liquid started leaking from the side and back of the machine. Not just a drip, a large amount of mix was constantly leaking out. lost $19.99 in margarita mix. The unit would not dispense anything. Hope this one is new and that it works. Needless to say we drank wine instead of margaritas for the party. HORRIBLE CHAIRS. Should have listened to the other reviews. These chairs are horrible. They make you lean in the forward position and are not very sturdy. I feel like I am falling out of the chair.

GOOD PRODUCT. I ordered these for extra hold for the command caddy. They work very well.

Work great. I use these hooks for everything. They are great. Mostly I have used them to hang and dry herbs from my garden for the winter. They worked out perfectly. I have also used them to hang item on the inside of my cabinet doors, which gives me more space usage.

Great decor for the price. I love these. Some of the green I had to put back in upon arrival but it still looks great.

Unfortunately we could not because our mantle is too big. Daughter in law didn't want them so we used them on our book racks for hanging dog stockings and a few other items. Worked well there.
You need to measure your mantle before buying, to save you a bit of grief.
the hooks are strong, concept is good, but unless there is weight on the hook (more than just a plain stocking) they will shift around.

Do not leave cover on if you are boiling water.. I love this little pot. It has replaced my egg cooker, frying pan and having to turn on the stove to make pasta. Soft, fluffy and gorgeous. Super quality and softness. I have used for a while now and it remains like new!

Oneida Dover Silverware not quality controlled. I needed to replace my Oneida Marquette 18/10 Silverware. I had it for 25 years and my daughter threw forks and spoons away as she was growing up. I did not notice until I had 3 teaspoons and 5 forks out of a set of 12. So I picked out Oneida Dover, it goes really nicely with my Mikasa Remembrance fine china. I ordered the 45 piece set it comes with some serving pieces. As you will see in the photos, there were problems. Salad Forks, Dinner Forks, Knifes, Diner Spoons and teaspoons all had missing or smuggled flowers on the handles. I called Oneida customer service. They said they are not aware of the problems. I sent them the photos and they checked there stock and found the same problems. They told me to call Amazon and return the silverware. This set was made in Indonesia. I am hoping in a few months the problem will be fix. If you look at Macy's the reviews are the same thing. Since November 2022 there is this problem. Oneida was sold to Lenox and Lenox was sold to someone else. The Molding/stamping has gone down hill.

Quality product, but a little hard to assemble. I never had an office chair that was quite as difficult to assemble as this was. I had to actually cut them off with a hacksaw to get them in far enough to get the trim strip to cover the heads. Also, I found it hard to attach the back; struggled with it for a while to get it positioned correctly. There are some extra screws included in case you lose one or more. Also, they include an Allen wrench to put the screws in with, so you don't need any other tools (unless you have to cut off some screws, as I did). The chair is adjustable on height, as almost all office chairs are. There is no adjustment on the arm height, but not expected for the price of the chair. Also note that the arms are a hard material and not padded. They seemed comfortable enough, but my current office chair has padded arms. The chair is basic black, but quite attractive. A good chair for the price. If you want more features, like adjustable arms, you will pay more. UPDATE: I have used this chair for a while now and find it to be very comfortable; more so than other chairs in the same price range. I am abandoning my old office chair and using this one exclusively now. 5 stars on comfort; the lumbar support is great.

The first thing I noticed about this blender is that the blending cup seemed very short and it seemed like it wouldn't hold as much as my other blender which hold 5 cups and is taller. This holds 6 cups and the reason it can hold more without as much height is that the blending cup is bigger around. The cup is nice thick glass and is one of the better features of the blender. The blender is attractive, with a silver colored base, but the base doesn't appear to be metal, but more like a pastic coated with silver material. Seems powerful enough to do most jobs, but probably more of a light duty blender. The wattage is 550, which seemed like a lot, but in checking other blenders some are in the 700 to 750 watt range and I'm sure they go higher as well. The gasket is not a separate piece which is a real plus. I suppose 12 speeds is nice, but how many speeds do you really need? I don't even use the 8 speeds on my old blender. Instructions say that to blend hot liquids you need to leave the cover loose and cover it with a towel. Seems like a hassle when other blenders will handle hot liquids without doing anything special. I usually don't read what other reviewers say, as I don't want to be influenced one way or another, but I noticed several who had a problem with the plastic blender cup base breaking easily. With a two year warranty and the low price of this blender, you probably can't go wrong, but it's not fun to wait for replacement parts. You also have to search for your receipt and whatever else might be required for warranty service or return. If I wanted a quality power tool, I wouldn't think twice about selecting Black & Decker as they make good power tools. Are their small appliances as good? Probably not. I recommend buying a blender from a manufacturer who has a long history of making quality blenders. Apparently Black & Decker acquired General Electric's small appliance division in 1984, so it would seem they have over 20 years of experience, but contrast this with the Waring Blender company that has been making blenders since the 1930's. There are so many blenders available in the market and there probably isn't a lot of difference amongst them until you start getting up into higher prices. Seems like there is a lot of competition in the market for blenders and this is a low end competitor is good enough for people who don't use a blender every day. If you are constantly using your blender (like for a daily smoothie), select something more rugged that costs more. This is by no means a food processor; I think it is wise to spend more and get a combo food processor and blender, which should serve your needs longer. A clever multitasker with easy cleanup...just don't go by the manual!. I've owned several George Foreman grills over the years, so I was thrilled that I had the chance to test out the Smart Kitchen Multicooker. My regular workhorse [[ASIN:B0007VZZNO Black & Decker HS1000 Handy Steamer with Flavor Scenter Screen]] was getting on in years, and was limited to steaming. However, the George Foreman Multicooker has a 5-quart capacity, and you can sear directly in the pan, then add your other ingredients to make stews, sauces, stir-fry, etc. Like the George Foreman grills, the nonstick coating allows for less oil or butter in cooking, cutting down on fat. There's also an adjustable steam vent on the lid. You can cook two things at once; for example, you can cook rice in the main pot while putting shrimp, fish, veggies, etc in the steamer basket above the rice, not only saving time but cutting down on dishes as well.

As other reviewers have mentioned, don't count on the included "instruction" manual for much guidance. In fact, if you relied on the manual alone, you probably wouldn't have much of a feel for the versatility of the product. It's a great help to watch the promo video on the official George Foreman website (see my post below for the URL). One thing I would have liked to have seen was a comprehensive list of steaming times for various ingredients similar to the manual from my old Black and Decker steamer (it included separate guides for meat, fish, veggies, frozen vs. fresh, etc.), although the Intelli-Probe digital controls have presets for rice and other settings. Another minus is the fittings for the steamer basket handles; these were roughly finished (it looked like the ends were clipped, resulted in sharp, uneven surfaces), and with frequent use I could see them scratching the nonstick coating of the pan.

Overall, this is a handy tool to have around the kitchen if you frequently cook large quantities of food since it has a 20-cup capacity, and being able to sear in the same pan is a great feature. However, the lack of suggested cooking times makes it a bit more difficult to use than a regular steamer.

A big step up from bargain toasters.... I spent years in graduate school making do with a five-dollar toaster. After moving into my first home, I decided it was definitely worth the splurge to upgrade to a toaster worthy of my homemade breads. I was given a KitchenAid 2-Slice Toaster as a housewarming gift, and the love affair hasn't stopped since.

The KitchenAid performs all the usual functions of a toaster, with many choices from light to dark, but also features a bagel setting designed to toast the cut side of bagels more thoroughly than the crust, and a "warm" setting to keep your toast warm without turning it into charcoal.

The toaster has a nice solid construction, with heavy-duty metal parts and a well-built crumb tray that slides out, eliminating the mess from trapdoor-style crumb trays found on cheaper toasters.

Since I bake my own bread, I tend to slice it thickly, and it turns out perfectly in the KitchenAid. But beware: if you use store-bought (or other thinly sliced) breads, the extra-wide slots mean that your toast may turn out very light and need an extra toasting since the bread is held further away from the heating elements. But it performs beautifully on bagels, English muffins, and thick slices of bread. Whoever said that man cannot live by bread alone failed to toast it in a KitchenAid toaster!

Pros
Toasts evenly, bagels come out perfectly done

Cons
Sometimes frozen breads require extra toasting, warming feature ineffective
