Tight Fit. I have a king size mattress. This mattress cover has a very tight fit. I couldn't get it to stay in place by myself and had to have my husband help me. With him on the opposite side, we were able to get it over all the corners. Once it was in place, it hasn't budged. We have had issues with our sheets staying in place over this. At least once or twice each night, I am having to adjust the sheet because I can't stand to have the corners of the sheet come up. I ordered this for the cooling effect. I haven't noticed much of that at all. When I first put it on, I noticed it "wasn't warm" like some covers, but it isn't cool either. I'm in my mid-50's and cooling would be nice. It definitely protects the mattress.

Fancy!. This is our 3rd air fryer. The first one we got was a bit small, so we upgraded to a larger one. I saw all the features that this one had and wanted to give it a try. This one has 2 baskets. The baskets are smaller than the single basket of the larger unit that we had. If it's just my husband and me, the smaller basket size is not a problem. If the kids are home from college, it will slow things down. This one allows you to do so much more than just air fry. We haven't quite figured out everything yet. There's definitely a learning curve and we're slowly figuring out how to use it. We like how it notifies you to shake the food. We made dinner tonight of french fries and chicken strips. The food turned out great! Though some how we turned it off or ended it during the middle of the cycle and had to restart it. That's where we're still learning. I do like that you can cook 2 separate foods at the same time. And it's nice to be able to view the food while it's cooking.

For the Price, It's a Good Deal. My son has always had an interest in rocks and minerals. He's finishing up college and has started purchasing some specimens. For the price, he says this is a good deal. The purple is a little lighter then he would prefer, but it's still attractive. He likes the really dark purple ones but those tend to cost more. He also liked that this one included a stand. He recently went to a rock and mineral show and spent hundreds of dollars on some beauties. This is also a decent size. His largest one weighs 34 pounds and cost over $400, so the price definitely increases as the size goes up. He is pleased with this amethyst and is happy to add it to his collection.

Bright Yellow. This is a good set of kitchen tools. There are 11 tools plus the storage holder. They are a very cheery, bright yellow color. The pieces are a mix of silicone and wood. Because of the wood, these items are recommended to be washed by hand. That's a strike against them. I am busy and need my utensils to go in the dishwasher! They seem to be sturdy and durable.

It Fits!. My daughter bought a cute stainless steel cup at Target a few months ago. She dropped it and the lid chipped. She said she would have kept using it except the chip was where you drink from and she didn't want to get cut. I measured the chipped lid and the cup opening. There were detailed measurements for this in the product description. I am happy to say that it fits! It's not particularly snug, but when turned over, the lid does not come out or move. The old lid had a slide piece that kept the drink from spilling. This one does not have any thing to keep it from spilling. She says that's okay. She's just happy to have a lid again!

Not Too Squishy. My 23 year old son was in need of a new mattress. He has difficulty sleeping and we were hoping a new mattress would help. He's a big guy. His previous mattress was a pillow top mattress. It was very squishy. This one is not too squishy - and I mean that in a good way. You do sink into it a little bit, but it's easy to get up out of it. You can feel support even though you've sunken down a little bit whereas the pillow top mattress did not feel supportive. The cooling effect is pretty mild. It may be that it's hard to go through the mattress protector and the sheets. It was noticeable before those pieces were put on it. He's been using it for a couple of nights now and so far, it doesn't seem to make any difference with his sleep. However, he does find it to be comfortable. He has an appointment with a sleep doctor soon, so hopefully that will help. The mattress arrived compressed and rolled up. It didn't take too long to fully expand - maybe a day. It didn't have any strong chemical smell like some memory foam products have.

Complete Set. This is a complete set of kitchen utensils, including a storage container. This would be good for someone just starting out. The pieces are decent, though the quality ranges on the individual items. They have silicone parts which seem to be rigid enough to function properly. They did have a strong odor when first opened, but I did wash them and that seem to take care of that. I couldn't find any care instructions either with the item or on the product description. I have been putting them in the dishwasher, so I hope that's okay!

Cute Table Runner. We have a bunch of cats in our house. They have started to infiltrate our Halloween decorations this year, too. So when I saw this cat themed Halloween table runner, I had to order it! It's a very cute Halloween design. It fits my table just fine. I had to take it back up after less than a day because one of our cats decided to lay on it and I didn't want it to get scratched or damaged. Most likely it would have gotten cat vomit or hairballs! I will put it back out on Halloween day. The quality is good. There's no backing to it.

Complete Bed in a Bag. Complete "bed in a bag" sets are great for a quick decorating change. This set includes sheets, pillow cases, shams and comforter. The items seem to be a decent quality, especially in the listed price range. I really like the floral print. I wouldn't call the pieces super soft, as the description states, but they're acceptable.

Nice Colors. I was intrigued with these stickers. I was drawn to the colors. I had never heard of the Lamare Habit tracker, so I looked it up and ended up ordering one so I could give it a try. The stickers are perfect for the tracker. I've only just started using it, but I am finding it a little tricky to remove the stickers. It's probably because they are small. It's not difficult, but it does require a little concentration. I've actually thought about using some flat craft tweezers if I can find mine to see if that helps at all. I really do like the look of them. They seem to stick well, but they are easy enough to lift up and reposition if you do it right away.

Looks Nice. This is a basic twin comforter. The description says it's "ultra soft", but I don't think it feels very soft at all. It's not rough to the touch either, but it's not what I would consider soft. The planets look nice. It's more of a realistic space depiction rather than cutesy. The quality seems to be okay, but it has the over all look and feel of an inexpensive comforter.

Good Lightweight Quilt. This is a good, decent light weight quilt. The material isn't super soft, but it's not rough or scratchy either. It's a good all seasons bed cover, though in the colder months, you may need an additional blanket. The quality is fine. The blue camouflage design is great for all ages.

Fits Twin Size Mattress. Mattress protectors are one of those most have items. This one is pretty basic, but it does do the job of protecting the mattress. It's for a guest bed that will be used by children, so it's more than fine. My own family members usually have the mattress protectors that have extra padding. This is terry material. It fits the twin size mattress fine. It's not what I would call noisy, but I wouldn't call it silent either. It doesn't make noise like the plastic ones, and that's what's important.

Cute Gnomes. Seasonal gnomes sure are popular these days! I couldn't help it and now I have a few different sets of them myself. These are primarily felt. They are a pretty good quality. I did find a loose thread on one and some glue was visible on the backside, but that's all. The arms and hats have wire inside so you can bend them. They are weighted on the bottom so they don't tip over easily. These are too big for my tiered tray, but they will be great on the mantle!

Frame Set. This holiday/seasonal decor has 3 rustic frames and a dozen double sided card stock images. I ordered this for my tiered trays. I have 2 trays, but I only use one at a time. It just depends on the size of the items and how much I have to put out. These are too big for the tray that I am currently using, but they do fit on my other one. The frames are wooden with plastic instead of glass. The plastic is covered in a protective film which has to be removed before using. I'm not really crazy about some of the cards though. I think they could have been nicer or prettier. Some of them look really good but some of them look more like they just stopped in the middle of designing them. It is a good deal to get all of these in a set.

Great for Tiered Trays!. I have discovered the art of decorating tiered trays and love how they look. Coffee is a big part of my life, so I thought a coffee themed one would be a good one to have in between seasons. These are great for the tiered trays! There are 3 blocks and a set of beads. Two of the blocks have wooden raised lettering which makes it look nicer. The overall quality of the items is very good. I am a bit confused with one of them. The one that says " I like my coffee (hot) & my f_____lly." I don't understand what it is. I've seen the saying, "I like my coffee hot, like my wife" or similar takes on that. This one has pictures of little houses instead of letters. I am guessing it's supposed to be family, but I'm not positive. Besides that, I am very pleased with these pieces and I look forward to creating my coffee themed tray soon.

Good Fit. These sheets are a good fit on my daughter's queen sized bed. They stay in place and don't roll off the corners, or at least they haven't yet! They do a have a cool feel to them, but they're not as soft as I would like. They're not rough or scratchy, but they do have a slick feel to them. They wash well. Overall, they're fine and good.

Looks Nice. This is a modern and updated tray table. It looks nice. Assembly was okay. My husband didn't have any major difficulties putting it together. However, he has lots of experience putting together box furniture. He did comment that it didn't seem as sturdy as some other pieces he's put together recently. With that being said, it is sturdy enough for a laptop or other fairly lightweight items. We have it set up in the basement where our 23 year son's room is. There are a couple of sofas down there where he will often hang out with his friends. This doesn't take up as much room as setting up a table for his guests.

So Far So Good. I haven't wanted a large clock for our living room for a while. I was a little worried when I received this because it was shipped in the product box which arrived pretty dinged up. The main part of it is pretty sturdy. The hands of the clock don't feel sturdy at all. They bend very easily. In fact, they were curved out more than they should have been. I adjusted them so it looked better. 1 AA battery is required (and not included). It has a little hanger on the back that was easy to hang on to an existing nail that was in our wall. So far, so good! It's been keeping time and it appears to be accurate. I can't say how accurate it is for certain. I am pleased with how it looks on the wall.

Looks Straight out of the 1970's!. This 1971 mug has a cute design. I think it looks straight out of the 1970's! It's pretty basic as far as the mug goes, but it will make a fun gift for someone turning 50 this year. It comes safely packaged.

Cute But Basic. This is a cute but basic lunch box. The Vera Bradley recycled cotton fabric is colorful. I appreciate that their new recycled cotton effort. The inside is just plain, easy to clean lining. There's a slip pocket for napkins and cutlery, but other than that there are no dividers. It would work well for sandwiches or flat containers, but it's not wide enough for larger containers. There's a clear name window on the outside.

Nice Looking Desk. My son is a college student studying IT. He also is a big gamer. He has a primary desk for his computer, but the top is taken up with all of his peripherals and accessories, that he doesn't have room left to write or do paper work. We put this desk next to his main desk to create an "L" shape work space. It is a nice looking desk. Since it doesn't have any shelves or drawers, it really could be used as just a work table. Assembly was straight forward and didn't take very long. My son is pleased with his new work space.

Lightly Scented. These candles are a good size. They have 3 wicks. The candles are lightly scented, but the scent is nice. I really like the orange blossom as it reminds me of Spain in the springtime. The candles have lids. The jars are nicely decorated. They seem to burn evenly. Overall, they are good.

Soft Blanket. I've been looking for a good blanket for our guest room. We have just a quilt on the bed in that room and an extra blanket would be nice. I didn't want something too thick and bulky. This is a thin blanket. It gives some additional warmth, though on a really cold night, you might prefer something heavier. The blanket is very soft. Construction seems to be good. It washes fine.

Customize Your Pillow. I like that you can actually customize your pillow to your preference. I've had a pillow that you could remove the stuffing to get it the right thickness, but that was a messy project. I had pillow fluff that I had to deal with. This is like having mini-flat pillows that you take out. I took out 3 of them and I have saved them in case I want to adjust the thickness again. The pillow is made well and I am very impressed with it. It's a comfortable fit for me!

Soft & Squishy. These feather pillows come compressed and rolled up. They expanded immediately after removing the plastic wrap. They are very soft and squishy. They don't have much support which is okay. I have a memory foam pillow for my head and then I use feather pillows to hug. I am using one of these and my son took the other. These pillows didn't have any odor or smell to them. The outer casing is very thick and nice.

Cute Finished Desk. Our daughter is in college. She is living on campus, but with the majority of her classes online this semester, she has been spending more time at home when her work schedule permits. The last time she was home, she complained about not having a desk in her room which made it difficult to study. She has a vanity in her bedroom, but the surface of that is too small to work and keep her laptop on it. This is a sturdy desk. It didn't take my husband too long to assemble. It does come with a small tool to put it together with, but my husband used his own tools, specifically his drill driver. Some of the holes in the desk don't line up, but overall, he got it together and it looks cute! I'm excited for her to see it the next time she comes home.

Good Size. I am trying to organize my home office/craft room. These containers are a good size. They can hold a lot as long as the contents aren't too heavy. The sides stay up at about 85-90% which is a little annoying. I wish they stayed up all the way because it looks nicer. The handles are sturdy. It came with stickers so you can label the contents, but the stickers don't stay in place very well. Overall, they're doing a good job helping with my organization.

Comfortable. These sheets are comfortable. They're not the softest microfiber sheets that I have used, but they're okay on the softness level. They fit my sleep number pillow top mattress without any problems. I had difficulties at first, trying to find the side that goes to the top of the bed. It's different than other top sheets. It's got a fold over part that reminds me more of a hotel sheet. There are 4 pillow covers that are more like shams than pillow cases. They are a little too big for my pillows - they might be king size and I don't have king size pillows. Overall, I am liking these sheets.

Sturdy. I really like this serving tray. It's very sturdy. The size is larger than I was anticipating, but for the better. We entertain outside a lot (because of the pandemic), so carrying items out on a tray is helpful. I did have difficulties removing the sticker. I had to soak it off and then use something to remove the remaining adhesive. Other than that, I am very pleased with it.

Cute But Pretty Basic. This is a cute black collage style frame, but pretty basic. It is primarily a table top frame. There is one picture hanging hook on the back off one of the individual frames, but it would take 2 to hang properly. Plus the back that does have the picture frame also has the stand attached to it. The picture hanger is on the bottom (middle) of the frame and if you turned it around so you could utilize the hanger, then the stand part hangs down. I do plan to hang it up on the wall but I will use Command strips to do so. The frames are plastic and pretty sturdy. Two of the corners are not glued well and have a gap. It is a nice way to display a grouping of photos.

Easy to Tip Over. This was quick and easy to assemble. Out of the box, it only took a few minutes for my husband to put it all together. The issue I have had with it is that the baskets can get knocked out of it a little to easily. My cat bunted the lower basket and one of the sides fell out its notch. It was easy to put back in place though. It also doesn't have a very large weight capacity. If you put items in the top basket and nothing in the lower ones, it tips over. The handle is merely for decoration. If you pull on it, it falls apart. It doesn't push well either. It looks good and if you find the right spot for it, I think it can be a decent storage unit.

Sheds white balls. Each and every time I wash this couch cover it sheds small white balls from the underneath gripping part that helps to hold it in place. This is so aggravating!! Other than that I Love how it feels!
Broke quickly. this brand is usually my favorite, however after a couple of uses this can opener started skipping, so I had to pry the lid up to shake food out
Larger than expected.. Larger than expected. Not that sturdy. Reasonably priced.
Not absorbent.. Not very absorbent. Very lightweight.
Cheaply made. Not worth the price. Flimsy

If it opened all the cans. If this opened all the cans it would be the best. But some small cans like tuna fish can it just doesn't open you need 2 or 3 passes to get it to open. I love the idea of this can opener.

When it was packaged the outer fan cover must have gotten pinched in the box well it so deformed now it will never fit the fan. Lasko fans are not what they once were. I will never buy another fan from them

No results seen on my hair. I actually do like how it feels when I go to sleep on this silk pillowcase, but unfortunately this pillowcase did not do anything for my hair. My hair feels the same like there was nothing special, it did feel like my face looked better, but not the hair.
Paper thin. Wasn't expecting a runner this thin inspite of the so called measurments in the description. Rubber underneath already pealing! Dollar store quality? and way overpriced
Washed up. These towels are made in India for the equivalent of a dollar ! WS probably laughing all the way to the bank..suckers that bought these for an absurd price!!
Not well made. Complicated small filling system. A bowl of water in the room might be simpler

Not as good as it looks in the picture. Wont stand or balance properly and the cap doesnt stay on tight/leaks. Very thin and flimsy stainless steel (if it is) ..Not satisfied at all as was intended to be a gift.

Cute design, but pretty useless as a rug. What a waste of money. These rugs attract cat hair like magic, and it's impossible to remove it from the type of fabric. Also, the rugs have some type of backing on them, but they do not adhere to my hardwood floors. Using them as food bowl pads right now instead of their original intended purpose as kitchen rugs.

good enough. it's dull, you'll have to push down really hard, perfect fit for pink lady apples from costco. I tried cutting bigger apples, the center core is too small, doesn't remove all the core, it cuts into it.

smaller than it appears. Chair is very well made! It is beautiful and the leather is very nice. I love the look of it and it appears well made.
The only con is it was rated for 400 lbs and it is too small for a large person. My husband and I only weigh 220 to 260 but it is too small for us to sit back and be comfortable and it is not wide enough for us so I cannot imaging someone 300 to 400 lbs being able to use it. Would be great for kids and smaller people.
Opposite of “luxury”.. “Luxury?” LMAO!!!!

Not the best juicer. At first I was excited, then I realized the cup for this was missing, well a cup should have been included according to the manual.
I started juicing, and right away particles were spitting everywhere from the back where the trash is supposed to be collected, creating more mess to clean up in the kitchen.
Honestly it wasn’t worth $70, I wish I would have just boxed it up and return it. Now I’m stuck with the annoying bulky mess machine.
It’s ok. Cute gag gift but the back piece keep falling off.

Need fingernails to open it. I had to send it back because my husband couldn't open it. I have slight nails and was able to slide them under the probe and lift it up. He was not able to do so. Instead we ordered the Harbor Instant Read Cooking Thermometer, which got good reviews and is similar looking but looks to have an easy lift probe. Not Great. Firstly, this is not a lunch box! It is massive! So no way is it good for portion control. Secondly, it leaks something terrible. I sent mine back almost right away as leaking lunchboxes are not my thing.

It won’t work if I just make one cup. It is pretty much impossible to clean by hand, has to be put in the dishwasher. Not very convenient while camping. Looks pretty but that’s about it.

FLIMSY AND NOT VERY STURDY. I USED THIS ONCE RIGHT AFTER I GOT IT AND I DONT CARE FOR IT. IT IS POOR PUT TOGETHER, IT IS FLIMSY, AND NOT VERY STURDY WHEN LAID DOWN FLAT (WOBBLES). I SHOULD HAVE SPENT THE EXTRA MONEY AND GOT SOMETHING A BIT BIGGER WITH BETTER QUALITY. THANKS.

Nice bowls. Pretty bowls. Well made. But the pouring design is lacking.. This is a pretty set, nice color, well made and very useable as bowls., However, the handle is too awkward to use for lifting and pouring, particularly given the weight of the bowls. I hefted an empty one and mimicked pouring and it's not convenient. Unlike a regular handle, it takes two hands to grasp and pour. If the contents were hot, it would particularly be a problem. The spout is broad and shallow. I withhold judgment but as a person who has cooked and baked for over fifty years, I'm expecting it won't pour as precisely as I'd like. I wanted these to be both pretty and practical. I don't really need more bowls. I wanted very effective, easy to manage pouring function.

Very Cute but cannot use washer or dryer to clean. I would expect a hand towel, even a cute cat novelty hand towel to be machine wash and dry. Particularly since I want to get germs out of it. This one must be hand washed in lukewarm water and dried in the shade. It only gets three stars because it is cute. Knowing the care instructions I will not acquire more.

Don't waste your money or your time on these.. I have week fingers due to arthritis. Can't lock my sheets in place. Finally removed them, attached the sheets and then installed them, but I am sure these will pop out because the piece that fits under the mattress is so short. Should have read the critical reviews.

It’s nice... but don’t wash with Clorox2 for colors!. Bought this for $22 in Used/Like New condition, otherwise I’d probably be really unhappy with it. Aesthetically, it’s pleasing to the eye—my 12 year old loves it. IMO, the teal-ish colored stripe is closer to light and darker variations of a royal blue, which still adds that pop of color, but it’s definitely not navy. I actually bought navy sheets with it after reading other reviews about the color and had to exchange them for gray because navy did NOT match. The plaid fabric is a little stiff but seems durable. My biggest complaint is that the solid gray back looks a little peachy tie-dye discolored after 1 wash using Clorox2 for colors, so I definitely don’t recommend using that product on it. Overall, for what I paid, and the fact that the back is hidden, it’s good.

Super thin. Doesn’t seem durable because it is so much thinner than the liner I was replacing, and the rings at the top are also on a very thin piece of plastic, which I’m assuming will be detaching soon due to the quality. Over all, I guess I got what I paid for.

Rough texture. Over-priced for the poor quality.. I was extremely disappointed with the quality of these washcloths. They have a very rough texture. It's very difficult to rinse the soap out of them, and due to the size and texture of the washcloth, it's very difficult to wring out the water from them.

I do NOT recommend.

Since the wire shelves DON'T have any special magical powers and they aren't capable of levitating on their own, I highly suggest that you purchase a shelf unit that does come with the hardware and support posts. ☺️

Fits Under Kitchen Cabinets, But Releases Steam While Brewing. This HAMILTON BEACH 12 CUP COMPACT PROGRAMMABLE COFFEE MAKER (Black with Stainless Steel Accents (46200)) really is compact--it fits under my kitchen cabinets with room to spare. However, it’s a good idea to pull it out from under the kitchen cabinets when you’re actually brewing coffee, because steam escapes from the top--especially if the coffee maker is in need of cleaning.

It makes good coffee, so I’m happy enough with it. I don’t use the programming feature--which other reviewers say will fail after a few months because steam gets into the display--so the coffee maker suits my needs. I truly hated a fancy Ninja coffee maker that was too tall to fit under my kitchen cabinets, because it hogged so much counter space.

The best coffeemaker that I’ve ever owned is this [[ASIN:B0844DSDBH Hamilton Beach Frontfill Deluxe Coffee Maker]], which fits under my kitchen cabinets, does NOT release steam while coffee is brewing, and is extremely easy to fill. If you can find one of these, it’s the one you should buy.

Other reviewers have complained about the inability to get replacement carafes for the Hamilton Beach coffee makers. This is true of virtually any brand of coffee maker. If you need a replacement carafe, you should ONLY buy a carafe that says it fits the particular brand and model number. The carafe lids on different models of the same brand have slightly different dome heights or configurations, so that the carafes are NOT interchangeable from model to model.

I’m okay with the carafe thing, as long as the coffee maker isn’t very expensive to begin with. It makes sense to simply buy a new coffee maker if you break the carafe, because the inexpensive models only last 2-3 years anyway.

EdgeKeeper Sheath Makes Carbon Steel Knife Special. It’s the “EdgeKeeper” sheath that makes this FARBERWARE 5252819 EDGEKEEPER BUTCHER KNIFE (7-Inch, Black) special. The sheath sharpens the blade every time that you insert or withdraw the knife, so there’s no need to mess with a sharpening steel to keep a good edge on the knife.

The knife itself is made of carbon steel, and has a hard plastic handle. It’s a decent knife, reasonably well balanced, and comfortable to hold. The edge is sharp, thanks to the EdgeKeeper sheath. However, the knife doesn't hold the edge well as you use it, so you need the sharpening sheath.

The knife is strictly hand-washable (use warm, soapy water). Wipe the blade dry immediately after washing, before replacing the knife in the sheath.

High-Quality Travel Pillow Is Difficult to Bag. This HAOBAIMEI TRAVEL NECK PILLOW (Memory Foam, Grey) is a high-quality, well-made travel pillow that can be positioned in myriad ways to support your head/neck comfortably in all kinds of seating. However, it’s bulky--about the size of a small loaf of bread when bagged. The bagged pillow is also an awkward shape (and a little heavy) to carry everywhere you go.

The memory foam provides solid support. However, the pillow is much more difficult to bag than the product video suggests. Bagging requires hand strength and sitting down so you can force the folded pillow into the bag.

A bonus thin sleep mask is included, but it isn’t very effective in blocking out light. It’s just a flat piece of padded black satin fabric.

Great “Hold” Feature, But Falls Short on “Instant Read”. This BEYOND GROUP 1 33 DIGITAL INSTANT READ THERMOCOUPLE THERMOMETER (with Folding Probe) has one great feature--a “Hold” button that locks the reading so you can read it after you remove the probe. However, it is NOT an “instant read” thermometer--when your fingers heat the probe a little by unfolding it, the display is very slow to return to a room temperature reading. Also, It takes many seconds to reach a stable reading after the probe is inserted into hot food.

The thermometer gives readings that are a couple of degrees higher than my expensive [[ASIN:B01M6V1SXE Thermapen]] (which does give instant readings). You’ll want to test this thermometer in boiling water, to determine what the degree readings really mean, if you’re planning to use it to test cooked meats for safety.

The default display shows Centigrade numbers; if you want Fahrenheit, you must press the “Hold” button for 3 seconds. You must reset to Fahrenheit frequently--whenever you power on the thermometer, and whenever it shuts off automatically (after a fairly short time).

The “Hold” button works as promised. When the temperature is locked, the display shows the last reading. (The display blinks when it’s reading temperatures.) However, the “Hold” feature isn’t enough to overcome the thermometer’s other deficiencies.

Square Candle Holders Are Too Small for U.S. Votive Candles, Tea Lights. These ROYAL IMPORTS GLASS VOTIVE CANDLE HOLDERS (European Style, Set of 6, Unfilled) are pretty--I love the square shape--but they’re too small for standard U.S. tea lights or votive candles. Lacks Automatic Air Quality Monitor Included in “Smart” Model. I ordered this GERMGUARDIAN AC4825 22" 3-IN-1 FULL ROOM AIR PURIFIER (HEPA Filter, UVC Sanitizer) for my home office because the fancier “smart” model (see [[ASIN:B01LCX9QWG Wi-Fi 4-in-1 GermGuardian]]) has performed so beautifully in my home. I have three of the “smart” air purifiers, in constant operation for more than a year, and none have presented any problems. They clean the air (odors and allergens), and the automatic air quality monitor (not included in this model) speeds up the fans when I cook something that smokes.

The wi-fi feature isn’t terribly useful, so I chose this 3-in-1 model for the additional room with the home office, not realizing that the air quality monitor was omitted (along with the wi-fi capability). The air quality monitor is a feature that matters to me, so this 3-in-1 model isn’t suitable to my needs.

More or Less Smokeless, But Many Things NOT to Like. This PHILIPS SMOKE-LESS GRILL (plus Bonus Cleaning Tool, HD6371/98) is very expensive (about $280 on Amazon) for what it is. It cooks with two banks of infrared lights, but that’s NOT why it’s “smokeless”.

It’s smokeless, more or less, because the drip tray is located well below the grill surface, and below the heat sources, so that grease drippings don’t burn hard onto the drip pan (causing smoke). If you’ve ever broiled a steak in an electric oven, you know that most of the smoke comes from grease that is burning onto the broiler pan surface nearest the broiler coils. Thus, with this grill, you’ll still get some smoke if you cook fatty foods.

My appliance didn’t melt at the sides with first use, but there are a lot of things to NOT like about this appliance. First, the handles on the barbecue grid (the loose tray on top) get very hot at the four points where the metal joins the plastic handle insulation. Surprise for the unwary cook!

Second, although there’s a warning against staring at the infrared lights, it’s impossible NOT to look at them, because they’re located right below the barbecue grid. You have to look down on them when you turn the food or check for doneness.

Third, the grill takes 6-7 minutes to preheat, and it sends a lot of heat into your kitchen. You definitely don’t want to use the appliance underneath your kitchen cabinets (danger of setting them on fire). My electric stove’s broiler doesn’t heat the kitchen as much. The appliance also takes quite a while to cool down so that it can be safely cleaned.

Fourth, the appliance is big and awkward to handle. It takes up a lot of countertop or table space.

Fifth, the drip tray slides out from the left end, so it needs a lot of space for removal.

Sixth, the appliance isn’t easy to clean, except for the barbecue grid and the drip tray (both are dishwasher safe). Grease spatters on the insides of the appliance, and must be scraped off. Otherwise, the grease will burn on and start to produce smoke.

Finally, the scraper tool is just a paint scraper with double-edged razor blades (you get three blades). These are readily available at hardware stores.

I’m still scratching my head at the price. I wanted this because my electric oven’s broiler produces some smoke, and because it burns grease onto the broiler pan so badly that I have to clean the pan with Easy-Off. But the broiler and broiler pan are much easier (and safer) to use and to clean than this grilling appliance.

Cleans Pod Capsule Only; Does Not Eliminate Need for Descaling. These KEURIG 5000057588 K-CUP COFFEE MAKER RINSE PODS (10 Count, White) only clean your coffee maker’s pod capsule—they are NOT a substitute for regular descaling of your entire coffee maker (see [[ASIN:B00FOT9W5Q Keurig Descaling Solution]]). The rinse pods cleanse the pod area (where you place the pods) and the channel below, to prevent “flavour carryover” between brews—especially between cups of hot chocolate, apple cider, or fancy flavored coffees and cups of plain coffee or tea.

To use the rinse pods, you need to (1) insert a rinse pod and brew a cup with water; (2) remove the used rinse pod and discard the rinse water; (3) rinse the pod capsule by brewing another cup with water only; and (4) discard the rinse water. In practice, I needed to rinse the pod capsule twice, because the first rinse produced a cup of hot rinse water with a white ring of chemicals around the water surface.

I think it’s easier to rinse the pod capsule (to reduce flavour carryover) by brewing one cup of plain water and discarding the rinse water. Doing it that way also avoids adding mildly toxic chemicals to your coffee maker.

The rinse pods contain maltodextrin, sodium bicarbonate, citric acid, and sodium citrate. The warning on the box says “do not consume”; and, among other things, advises you to “Seek medical attention if a large amount is swallowed, if irritation persists, or if you feel unwell.”

Medium-Sized-Room Humidifier Has All Desirable Features. UPDATE 3/12/18: After several months of uneventful operation, my humidifier began intermittently leaking badly onto the floor. I finally figured out that the water reservoir in the base, which hydrates the wick, was overfilling. This was happening because the valve on the refillable water tank, which controls the automatic delivery of water as needed during operation, was malfunctioning. This was NOT user error. It is a basic design or manufacturing flaw. Rating changed from 5 stars to 1 star.

This VORNADO ENERGY SMART EVAPORATIVE HUMIDIFIER (EVDC300, with Automatic Shut-off, 1 Gallon Capacity, LED Display) has all the features that I want in a medium-room-size humidifier. First, when it's running in the “Energy Smart” mode (indicated by a green light next to the lighted power button), it turns off automatically when it runs out of water.

Second, it remembers the settings when it's turned off. After you power it off and on again while refilling the tank, you don't have to punch all the buttons again for (1) humidity level, (2) fan speed, and (3) automatic, continuous, or Energy Smart mode.

Third, it has a 1-gallon tank that lasts about 30 hours (when I keep it in Energy Smart mode, on high fan speed, with 60% humidity). The tank is easy to refill, because it has a wide circular top opening, and isn't too heavy when filled with water. The tank has a built-in handle that makes it easy to carry.

Fourth, it has a single wick (a mesh sheet that soaks up water from the tank). This needs to be replaced when it gets hard enough that it won’t wick up water, or when it develops algae or mold. The wick contains an antimicrobial additive, and you can extend the wick’s life by adding a bacteriostatic solution that suppresses algae growth to the water tank. The wick is supposed to last 4-8 weeks; using the algae suppressant, my wicks last at least 12 weeks (in Energy Smart mode). (This model uses [[ASIN:B01J664VSA Vornado EVDC300 wicks (2-pack)]].)

Fifth, the fan turns off when the humidifier sensor determines that the set humidity level has been reached. You can set the humidity at anything from 40 to 60 percent (in 5-point steps). The sensor is an approximation, of course--when my humidifier reads 60%, two other nearby sensors read 46% and 56%. It takes a few days for the room humidity to reach the desired level. (The fan can be manually set to run continuously at extra-high speed, if you want to raise the humidity level fast. If you do this, check the water tank frequently, because with this setting the humidifier won't turn off automatically when it’s out of water.)

Finally, the humidifier has a water tank light that pulses a warning when the water level is low.

The organizer also gets in the way of your bedcovers, unless you install it at the very head of the bed. I was hoping to use this organizer to hold things that wouldn't fit on my crowded bedside table, but it's too inconvenient for regular use. InterDesign products are usually much nicer than this one.

Fabulous Looks, But Overall Poor Design. This MR.COFFEE 12-CUP PROGRAMMABLE COFFEEMAKER, STAINLESS STEEL looks fabulous, brews fast, has easy-to-use buttons, includes a water filtration system, has a keep-warm plate, and includes a cleaning cycle setting. Unfortunately, the coffeemaker also has a hard-to-fill reservoir, a clumsy "removable filter basket", and an exposed showerhead-type water system that emits steam when the lid is opened.

The good looks are not enough to make me like this coffeemaker! Everything (coffee grounds and water) must be added from the top. This is all right when the coffeemaker is cold. However, if you open the top to add coffee for a second pot right after the first pot has brewed, the showerhead will send a cloud of steam straight into your face. (I strongly prefer a coffeemaker with an enclosed showerhead and a coffee basket that swings out sideways, like the slower-brewing [[ASIN:B0041A5H5S Hamilton Beach 12-Cup Digital Coffee Maker]].)

The lid on this Mr. Coffee coffeemaker has a second lid in the back half that flips up. I think this is intended for you to use in filling the reservoir, but the second lid doesn't always want to stay up. It's also faster to fill the reservoir by opening the entire lid. When you open the top, the entire mechanism with the showerhead feels flimsy, as if it will break easily (and early breakage has been my experience with this type of coffeemaker design).

The outer "removable filter basket" lacks a handle for easy removal. It has ear-like tabs that are hard to grip (especially if the coffeemaker is hot) and require using two hands to pull the basket up and out. If you're using the water filtration system, you will probably want to remove this outer basket for every pot, because you must put ground coffee (inside a paper or permanent filter) into the basket, and then place the water filtration system over the top of the basket. The water filtration system itself consists of a charcoal filter disk that slides into a frame or lid for the "removable filter basket".

The water filtration system is supposed to remove chlorine from your water, to make your coffee taste better. You need to change the charcoal filter every month. (The coffeemaker comes with just one filter.) This isn't very useful to me, because my tap water often tastes odd because of organic matter. Removing chlorine isn't enough, so I filter my coffee water with a different type of filter before adding it to the coffeemaker's water reservoir.

My coffeemaker arrived without either paper filters or the "Mr. Coffee nylon permanent filter" that is supposed to be included (according to the instructions). I guess that the permanent filter got removed in the warehouse, because the box wasn't completely sealed when it arrived. Some kind of additional filter is needed inside the "removable filter basket", or coffee grounds will escape into the carafe during brewing.

The coffeemaker comes with a short 26" cord, which is more or less standard for kitchen appliances now, especially heating appliances. The cord arrives coiled inside the coffeemaker's base, and needs to be pulled out when you first set up the coffeemaker.

Because of the many bad design features, I rate it this Mr. Coffee coffeemaker (Model BVMC-JPX37-AM) at 2 stars ("I don't like it" on the official Amazon scale).

Beautiful Cookware That Requires Special Care to Keep Its Looks. This ALL-CLAD MC2 PROFESSIONAL MASTER CHEF 7-PIECE COOKWARE SET is drop-dead gorgeous. It is meticulously designed, machined, and hand-finished. However, it's a poor choice for me, because (1) my kitchen has a ceramic-top electric range, (2) it's heavier than my all-stainless-steel cookware, and (3) it requires hand-washing and a lot of extra care to keep it looking beautiful.

In general, aluminum cookware is the most energy-efficient, which is why "stainless steel" cookware usually has an aluminum core. Aluminum cookware is also lightweight. However, cookware made entirely from aluminum poses some toxic risk in regular use, because minute amounts of aluminum can leach into food during cooking (particularly into acidic foods like tomatoes).

This All-Clad cookware has a stainless steel interior that won't react with food. Thus it's completely safe for all cooking. It cooks efficiently, because it has an all-aluminum core plus an all-aluminum brushed exterior. However, it isn't particularly lightweight. The 9-inch All-Clad frying pan from this set weighs 1 lb. 9.9 oz., while my 9-inch Cuisinart stainless steel frying pan with aluminum-core bottom weighs 1 lb. 6.6 oz.

My ceramic-top electric range is not friendly to aluminum cookware, because aluminum has a fairly low melting point. The manual for the electric range suggests using extra caution when cooking with aluminum cookware, because aluminum can leave scuff marks on the cooktop, and because a pan allowed to boil dry can melt, fuse with the cooktop, and severely damage the cooktop. Of course it's fine to use this All-Clad cookware on a ceramic-top stove, but the cook needs to exercise particular care (1) to never turn the heat on under an empty pan, and (2) to follow the All-Clad recommendation and always use low or medium heat, except when boiling water. (The recommendation to use low or medium heat is NOT just for ceramic-top ranges, because high heat can warp any cookware.)

However, the main reason that I'm disappointed with this All-Clad cookware is that it requires so much extra care to maintain its stunning appearance. The All-Clad instructions include the following cautions: (1) to avoid the formation of white dots or pits in the cookware, bring water to a boil or wait for foods to begin cooking before adding salt; (2) to prevent water spotting, rinse in hot water and dry immediately; and (3) to prevent discoloration, avoid overheating (produces brown or blue spots), remove food films before reheating, and avoid high-iron-content water. In addition, for ordinary cleaning, the stainless steel interior should be cleaned with a paste of fine powder cleanser, washed in hot soapy water, and dried immediately. (You musn't use oven cleaners, oven cleansers, or chlorine bleach.) The aluminum MC2 exterior should be cleaned with commercial aluminum cleaner, and rinsed in lukewarm water.

In short, this cookware is "not recommended for dishwasher use". Because this All-Clad cookware is beautiful, but requires pampering to stay that way, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

Well-Made, Works Well, But Not Best Available Corn Stripper Tool. If it weren't so fiddly to use, I would really love this RSVP SHUCK DELUXE CORN STRIPPER. The product's clear plastic outer tube is both its best and its worst feature. The best, because the tube catches all of the stripped corn kernels, and is easy to empty. The worst, because the tube must be opened and closed for every single ear of corn; each ear of corn must be carefully positioned inside the tube; and the yellow cap at the bottom of the tube has screw threads that run in the "wrong" direction. (To unscrew something, the mantra is "righty tightey, lefty loosey"--but this tube opens when turned right, and closes when turned left. Probably it's designed this way so it won't unscrew when the corer is twisted.)

The stainless steel "corer" is sharp, and it cuts the kernels off the cob with very little downward pushing effort. However, it misses all the kernels at the narrow end of the ear. The gadget is a little confusing at first, but simple to use once you understand how it works. You cut the kernels off by twisting the scalloped yellow part that's attached to the stainless steel corer; then you use the knobbed yellow part to push the stripped cob out of the corer. It's easiest if you take the knobbed part out before you strip the corn kernels off the cob. All of the corn stripper parts are sturdy, and they are all dishwasher safe.

This RSVP Corn Stripper is slightly more efficient than my [[ASIN:B000V78JGO OXO Good Grips Corn Stripper]], which has to be emptied several times for each ear of corn, and is a bit awkward to take apart and reassemble each time. However, my favorite tool for this job is the [[ASIN:B006GDRD9G Zyliss Corn Stripper]], which strips an entire ear of corn completely with 4 or 5 quick downward strokes (when you hold an ear of corn over a bowl or plate, you don't need either a tube (RSVP) or a container (OXO) to catch the stripped kernels).

Because it's fiddly and not the best available tool for the job, I rate this well-made product at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

Don't expect much. We have four mostly-indoor pets, and now that it's almost spring, the shedding has gotten out of control. I'm disappointed this isn't a slightly more robust vacuum, but I suppose the cheap price indicates what you can really expect from this.
